title: ENGLISH TENSES: COMPLETE GUIDE
notes:
✓ Tense → a grammatical system used to express the time and aspect of an action, event, or state.

◆ Three basic time references → Present, Past, Future.

◆ Four aspects → Simple, Continuous, Perfect, Perfect Continuous.

◆ Main combinations → 3 time references × 4 aspects = 12 traditional English tenses.

✓ Tense helps show → when something happens, whether it is repeated or temporary, whether it is completed, and how long it continues.

✓ Basic verb forms → V1 = base form, V2 = past simple, V3 = past participle, V-ing = present participle.

title: THE FOUR ASPECTS
notes:
◆ SIMPLE → presents an action, event, habit, fact, or state as a whole.
🔹 She works every day.

◆ CONTINUOUS → presents an action as being in progress around a particular time.
🔹 She is working now.

◆ PERFECT → connects an earlier event with a later reference point.
🔹 She has finished her work.

◆ PERFECT CONTINUOUS → emphasizes the duration or ongoing nature of an activity up to a reference point.
🔹 She has been working for three hours.

✓ Memory → Simple = fact/action | Continuous = in progress | Perfect = completed/connected | Perfect Continuous = duration.

title: PRESENT SIMPLE: FORMATION
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + V1/V1+s(es).

🔹 I work. / You work. / We work. / They work.
🔹 He works. / She works. / It works.

✓ Negative → Subject + do/does + not + V1.
🔹 I do not work.
🔹 He does not work.

✓ Yes/No question → Do/Does + subject + V1?
🔹 Do you work here?
🔹 Does she work here?

✓ Wh-question → Wh-word + do/does + subject + V1?
🔹 Where does he live?

⚠ After does/doesn't, never add -s to the main verb.
❌ Does she works?
✓ Does she work?

title: PRESENT SIMPLE: COMPLETE USES
notes:
◆ 1. Habits and repeated actions → I exercise every morning.

◆ 2. Permanent or relatively stable situations → She lives in Addis Ababa.

◆ 3. General truths → Water boils at 100°C at sea level.

◆ 4. Scientific facts → The Earth revolves around the Sun.

◆ 5. States → I understand the question.

◆ 6. Opinions, feelings, possession, and relationships → I believe you. / He owns a car.

◆ 7. Regular schedules → The class starts at 8:00.

◆ 8. Timetables and official programs → The plane leaves at noon.

◆ 9. Instructions and directions → You turn left at the junction.

◆ 10. Narratives and summaries → The hero enters the room and discovers a letter.

◆ 11. Headlines → Government announces new policy.

◆ 12. Zero conditional → If you heat ice, it melts.

✓ Common expressions → always, usually, normally, generally, often, frequently, sometimes, occasionally, rarely, seldom, hardly ever, never, every day/week/year.

title: PRESENT SIMPLE: SPELLING RULES
notes:
◆ Most verbs → add -s.
play → plays
read → reads
work → works

◆ Verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -z, -o → usually add -es.
watch → watches
wash → washes
go → goes
fix → fixes

◆ Consonant + y → change y to i and add -es.
study → studies
try → tries

◆ Vowel + y → simply add -s.
play → plays
enjoy → enjoys

⚠ Have → has.
He has a car.

⚠ Be is irregular → I am, you/we/they are, he/she/it is.

title: PRESENT CONTINUOUS: FORMATION
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + am/is/are + V-ing.

🔹 I am working.
🔹 He is working.
🔹 They are working.

✓ Negative → Subject + am/is/are + not + V-ing.
🔹 She is not sleeping.

✓ Question → Am/Is/Are + subject + V-ing?
🔹 Are they studying?

✓ Wh-question → Wh-word + am/is/are + subject + V-ing?
🔹 What are you doing?

✓ The auxiliary verb changes; the main verb remains in -ing form.

title: PRESENT CONTINUOUS: COMPLETE USES
notes:
◆ 1. Action happening at the moment → I am writing now.

◆ 2. Action happening around the present period → I am studying for my exams this month.

◆ 3. Temporary situations → She is staying with her friend this week.

◆ 4. Changing or developing situations → The climate is becoming warmer.

◆ 5. Repeated irritating behavior with always → He is always losing his keys.

◆ 6. Temporary trends → More people are using electric vehicles.

◆ 7. Definite future arrangements → We are meeting tomorrow.

◆ 8. Actions occurring during a particular period → They are building a new school.

✓ Expressions → now, right now, at the moment, currently, today, this week, this month, these days.

title: PRESENT CONTINUOUS: -ING SPELLING
notes:
◆ Most verbs → add -ing.
work → working
read → reading

◆ Verbs ending in silent -e → remove e.
make → making
write → writing
come → coming

◆ Verbs ending in -ee → usually retain the e.
see → seeing
agree → agreeing

◆ Short stressed vowel + consonant → often double final consonant.
run → running
sit → sitting
stop → stopping

◆ Verbs ending in -ie → change ie to y.
lie → lying
die → dying
tie → tying.

title: PRESENT PERFECT: FORMATION
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + have/has + V3.

🔹 I have finished.
🔹 She has finished.

✓ Negative → Subject + have/has + not + V3.
🔹 They have not finished.

✓ Question → Have/Has + subject + V3?
🔹 Have you finished?

✓ Wh-question → Wh-word + have/has + subject + V3?
🔹 Where have you been?

✓ The present perfect links a past event to the present rather than simply placing it at a finished past time.

title: PRESENT PERFECT: COMPLETE USES
notes:
◆ 1. Past action with present result → I have lost my keys. (I do not have them now.)

◆ 2. Life experience → She has visited Kenya three times.

◆ 3. Recently completed action → He has just arrived.

◆ 4. Unfinished time period → I have read two chapters today.

◆ 5. Repeated actions up to the present → We have watched that movie several times.

◆ 6. Situation continuing from past to present → They have lived here for ten years.

◆ 7. News and recent events → The team has won the match.

◆ 8. With superlatives and expressions such as first/second time → This is the best film I have ever seen.

✓ Common expressions → already, just, yet, ever, never, recently, lately, so far, until now, up to now, this week, today, since, for.

⚠ Finished-time expressions such as yesterday, last year, two days ago, and in 2019 normally require Past Simple.

title: PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS: FORMATION
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + have/has + been + V-ing.

🔹 I have been studying.
🔹 She has been working.

✓ Negative → Subject + have/has + not + been + V-ing.

✓ Question → Have/Has + subject + been + V-ing?
🔹 Have you been waiting long?

✓ Main emphasis → duration, continuity, or evidence of a recent activity.

title: PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS: COMPLETE USES
notes:
◆ 1. Action that started in the past and continues now → I have been studying since morning.

◆ 2. Action recently stopped with visible evidence → She is tired because she has been running.

◆ 3. Emphasis on duration → They have been waiting for two hours.

◆ 4. Repeated or temporary activity over a period → He has been working hard lately.

✓ Common expressions → for, since, all day, all morning, lately, recently, how long.

⚠ Stative verbs are normally not used in this tense.
❌ I have been knowing him for years.
✓ I have known him for years.

title: PRESENT PERFECT VS PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Present Perfect → emphasizes result, completion, achievement, or number.
🔹 I have written five pages.

✓ Present Perfect Continuous → emphasizes activity or duration.
🔹 I have been writing for two hours.

🔹 I have painted the room. → focus on completed result.
🔹 I have been painting the room. → focus on activity/process.

⚠ Some verbs strongly prefer Present Perfect because they describe states or completed situations.

title: PAST SIMPLE: FORMATION
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + V2.

🔹 I worked. / She went.

✓ Negative → Subject + did not + V1.
🔹 I did not work.
🔹 She did not go.

✓ Question → Did + subject + V1?
🔹 Did you work yesterday?

✓ Wh-question → Wh-word + did + subject + V1?
🔹 Where did they go?

⚠ After did/didn't, always use V1.
❌ Did he went?
✓ Did he go?

title: PAST SIMPLE: COMPLETE USES
notes:
◆ 1. Completed action → I finished my homework.

◆ 2. Action at a definite past time → She arrived yesterday.

◆ 3. Series of completed actions → He woke up, ate breakfast, and left.

◆ 4. Past habits → We played football every weekend.

◆ 5. Past states → I lived there when I was young.

◆ 6. Historical events → Ethiopia joined the League of Nations in 1923.

◆ 7. Narratives and stories → The king entered the hall and spoke to the crowd.

◆ 8. Second conditional result clauses → If I had enough money, I bought... (⚠ normally use would in the result; see conditional rules).

✓ Expressions → yesterday, last night/week/year, ago, in 2010, when I was young, once, then, afterwards.

title: PAST SIMPLE: REGULAR AND IRREGULAR VERBS
notes:
◆ Regular verbs usually form V2 with -ed.
work → worked
play → played
visit → visited

◆ Verbs ending in consonant + y → y becomes i + ed.
study → studied
try → tried

◆ Short stressed vowel + consonant → often double consonant.
stop → stopped
plan → planned

◆ Irregular verbs must be learned individually.
go → went
see → saw
eat → ate
write → wrote
take → took
come → came
buy → bought
teach → taught.

title: PAST CONTINUOUS: FORMATION
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + was/were + V-ing.

🔹 I was working.
🔹 They were working.

✓ Negative → Subject + was/were + not + V-ing.

✓ Question → Was/Were + subject + V-ing?
🔹 Were you sleeping?

✓ Wh-question → Wh-word + was/were + subject + V-ing?
🔹 What were they doing?

title: PAST CONTINUOUS: COMPLETE USES
notes:
◆ 1. Action in progress at a particular past time → At 8 p.m., I was studying.

◆ 2. Longer background action interrupted by a shorter event → I was sleeping when the phone rang.

◆ 3. Two simultaneous actions → While she was cooking, I was studying.

◆ 4. Temporary past situation → He was living in Addis Ababa at that time.

◆ 5. Background description in narratives → The sun was shining and people were walking through the streets.

✓ Common connectors → while, when, as, at that moment, at 5 p.m. yesterday.

title: PAST PERFECT: FORMATION AND USE
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + had + V3.

✓ Negative → Subject + had not + V3.

✓ Question → Had + subject + V3?

✓ Use → shows that one past action happened before another past action or past reference point.

🔹 When I arrived, the train had left.

✓ Time order → Earlier past = Past Perfect → Later past = Past Simple.

✓ Common expressions → before, after, already, by the time, until then, when.

⚠ Past Perfect is especially useful when the order of two past events might otherwise be unclear.

title: PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + had + been + V-ing.

✓ Negative → Subject + had not + been + V-ing.

✓ Question → Had + subject + been + V-ing?

✓ Use → emphasizes the duration or continuing activity before another past event.

🔹 They had been waiting for two hours when the bus arrived.

🔹 She was tired because she had been working all day.

✓ Focus → duration/process before a past reference point.

✓ Expressions → for, since, before, until, by the time, how long.

title: PAST PERFECT VS PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Past Perfect → emphasizes completed action/result.
🔹 She had cleaned the house before the guests arrived.

✓ Past Perfect Continuous → emphasizes duration/activity.
🔹 She had been cleaning the house for three hours before the guests arrived.

✓ Result vs duration → Past Perfect = what had happened; Past Perfect Continuous = how long it had been happening.

title: FUTURE SIMPLE WITH WILL
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + will + V1.

✓ Negative → Subject + will not + V1.
🔹 will not = won't.

✓ Question → Will + subject + V1?

✓ Major uses → spontaneous decisions, promises, offers, requests, predictions, willingness, refusals, and future facts.

◆ Spontaneous decision → The phone is ringing. I will answer it.
◆ Promise → I will help you.
◆ Prediction → I think it will rain tomorrow.
◆ Offer → I will carry your bag.

⚠ Will does not normally follow an if-clause in ordinary first conditional sentences.
❌ If it will rain, we will stay home.
✓ If it rains, we will stay home.

title: FUTURE CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + will + be + V-ing.

✓ Negative → Subject + will not + be + V-ing.

✓ Question → Will + subject + be + V-ing?

✓ Use → an action that will be in progress at a particular future time.

🔹 This time tomorrow, I will be travelling.

🔹 At 9 p.m., she will be studying.

✓ Other use → polite questions about someone's plans without implying a request.
🔹 Will you be using the computer this evening?

✓ Expressions → this time tomorrow, at 8 p.m. tomorrow, next week at this time.

title: FUTURE PERFECT
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + will + have + V3.

✓ Negative → Subject + will not + have + V3.

✓ Question → Will + subject + have + V3?

✓ Use → action completed before a specified future time or event.

🔹 By Friday, I will have finished the project.

🔹 By the time you arrive, we will have eaten dinner.

✓ Focus → completion before a future deadline.

✓ Expressions → by, by then, by tomorrow, by next month, by the time, before.

title: FUTURE PERFECT CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Positive → Subject + will + have + been + V-ing.

✓ Negative → Subject + will not + have + been + V-ing.

✓ Question → Will + subject + have + been + V-ing?

✓ Use → emphasizes how long an activity will have continued up to a future point.

🔹 By June, I will have been studying English for three years.

🔹 By 10 p.m., she will have been working for eight hours.

✓ Focus → duration leading up to a future reference point.

✓ Expressions → for, since, by, by the time, by next year.

title: BE GOING TO
notes:
✓ Form → Subject + am/is/are + going to + V1.

✓ Use 1 → prior plans or intentions.
🔹 I am going to study tonight.

✓ Use 2 → predictions based on present evidence.
🔹 Look at those dark clouds. It is going to rain.

✓ Negative → I am not going to go.

✓ Question → Are you going to study?

✓ Difference from will → going to often indicates an existing intention or evidence-based prediction; will often indicates a spontaneous decision, promise, or general prediction.

title: PRESENT CONTINUOUS FOR FUTURE
notes:
✓ Form → am/is/are + V-ing.

✓ Use → definite personal arrangements, usually with a future time expression.

🔹 I am meeting my teacher tomorrow.
🔹 We are travelling next week.

✓ Difference → emphasizes that the arrangement has already been made.

🔹 I am meeting John tomorrow. → arrangement.
🔹 I am going to meet John tomorrow. → intention/plan.
🔹 I will meet John tomorrow. → future decision/prediction or neutral statement.

title: PRESENT SIMPLE FOR FUTURE TIMETABLES
notes:
✓ Present Simple can describe future events that are fixed by a timetable, schedule, program, or calendar.

🔹 The train leaves at 7 tomorrow.
🔹 The semester begins next Monday.
🔹 The exam starts at 9 a.m.

✓ Comparison → Present Simple = official schedule | Present Continuous = personal arrangement | going to = intention/evidence | will = decision/prediction/promise.

title: FUTURE TIME CLAUSES
notes:
✓ After time expressions such as when, before, after, as soon as, until, once, and unless, English normally uses Present Simple to refer to the future in the subordinate clause.

✓ I will call you when I arrive.
❌ I will call you when I will arrive.

✓ We will start after he comes.

✓ Wait here until I return.

⚠ The main clause can contain a future form while the time clause uses Present Simple.

title: TENSE COMPARISON: PRESENT SIMPLE VS PRESENT CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Present Simple → routine, repeated, permanent, or general situation.
🔹 She works in a bank.

✓ Present Continuous → temporary or current activity.
🔹 She is working from home this week.

🔹 I read every night. → habit.
🔹 I am reading now. → current activity.

🔹 The Earth moves around the Sun. → fact.
🔹 The company is expanding rapidly. → developing situation.

title: PRESENT PERFECT VS PAST SIMPLE
notes:
✓ Present Perfect → past connected to present; finished time is not specified.
🔹 I have visited Nairobi.

✓ Past Simple → completed event at a finished past time.
🔹 I visited Nairobi last year.

⚠ Finished time → Past Simple.
🔹 yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago.

⚠ Unfinished period → Present Perfect may be used.
🔹 I have spoken to him twice today. (today is not finished.)

title: PAST SIMPLE VS PAST CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Past Simple → completed event.
🔹 I watched a movie.

✓ Past Continuous → activity in progress at a past time.
🔹 I was watching a movie at 8 p.m.

✓ Combined → I was watching a movie when my friend called.

✓ Common pattern → Past Continuous = background/longer action; Past Simple = shorter/interruption event.

title: PAST SIMPLE VS PAST PERFECT
notes:
✓ Past Simple → sequence of past events.
🔹 I arrived and she left.

✓ Past Perfect → makes an earlier past event explicit.
🔹 She had left before I arrived.

✓ Time order → had left = first event; arrived = second event.

⚠ If words such as before/after already make the sequence perfectly clear, Past Perfect may sometimes be unnecessary, but it is useful for emphasizing the earlier event.

title: FUTURE SIMPLE VS FUTURE CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Future Simple → future action, decision, promise, prediction, or event.
🔹 I will study tomorrow.

✓ Future Continuous → action that will be in progress at a particular future time.
🔹 I will be studying at 8 tomorrow.

✓ Difference → will study = future event; will be studying = activity in progress at a future reference time.

title: FUTURE PERFECT VS FUTURE PERFECT CONTINUOUS
notes:
✓ Future Perfect → emphasizes completion.
🔹 By June, I will have finished the course.

✓ Future Perfect Continuous → emphasizes duration.
🔹 By June, I will have been studying for two years.

✓ Completion vs duration → Perfect = result; Perfect Continuous = length of activity.

title: STATIVE VERBS
notes:
✓ Stative verbs describe states rather than actions and are generally not used in continuous forms.

◆ Mental states → know, understand, believe, remember, forget, mean, realize, suppose.

◆ Feelings/preferences → love, hate, like, dislike, want, need, prefer.

◆ Perception → see, hear, smell, taste, seem.

◆ Possession/relationship → own, belong, have (possession), contain, consist.

✓ I know the answer.
❌ I am knowing the answer.

✓ She owns a car.
❌ She is owning a car.

⚠ Some verbs change meaning and can therefore be continuous.
🔹 I think he is honest. → opinion.
🔹 I am thinking about the problem. → mental activity.

🔹 I have a car. → possession.
🔹 I am having lunch. → activity.

title: SINCE, FOR, AGO AND DURING
notes:
◆ Since → starting point.
🔹 since Monday, since 2020, since morning.

◆ For → duration.
🔹 for two hours, for five years.

◆ Ago → amount of time before now or a past reference point.
🔹 I met him two years ago.

◆ During → within a period/event.
🔹 I met many people during the trip.

⚠ Since and for are especially common with Perfect and Perfect Continuous forms.

title: WHEN, WHILE, AS, BEFORE AND AFTER
notes:
◆ When → can connect events occurring at or around a particular time.
🔹 I was sleeping when the phone rang.

◆ While → commonly introduces an action in progress.
🔹 While I was studying, she was cooking.

◆ As → similar to while when two activities develop simultaneously.
🔹 As I was walking home, it started raining.

◆ Before → earlier event.
🔹 She had left before I arrived.

◆ After → later event.
🔹 After he had finished, he went home.

title: USED TO, WOULD AND PAST HABITS
notes:
✓ Used to + V1 → past habits or past states that are no longer true.
🔹 I used to live in Hawassa.
🔹 She used to play tennis.

✓ Would + V1 → repeated past actions, especially in stories.
🔹 Every summer, we would visit our grandparents.

⚠ Would is normally not used for past states.
❌ I would know him when I was young.
✓ I used to know him when I was young.

✓ Used to can express both past states and repeated actions; would mainly expresses repeated actions.

title: CONDITIONALS AND TENSES
notes:
◆ Zero Conditional → If + Present Simple, Present Simple.
🔹 If you heat water, it boils.

◆ First Conditional → If + Present Simple, will + V1.
🔹 If it rains, we will stay home.

◆ Second Conditional → If + Past Simple, would + V1.
🔹 If I had more money, I would travel.

◆ Third Conditional → If + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
🔹 If I had studied, I would have passed.

◆ Mixed Conditional → combines different time references.
🔹 If I had studied harder, I would have a better job now.

⚠ Important → Do not normally use will directly after if in ordinary conditional clauses.

title: TENSES IN REPORTED SPEECH
notes:
✓ When a reporting verb is in the past, the original tense may shift backward.

◆ Present Simple → Past Simple.
🔹 Direct: “I work here.”
🔹 Reported: He said that he worked there.

◆ Present Continuous → Past Continuous.
🔹 “I am studying.” → She said she was studying.

◆ Present Perfect → Past Perfect.
🔹 “I have finished.” → He said he had finished.

◆ Past Simple → Past Perfect.
🔹 “I went home.” → She said she had gone home.

◆ Will → Would.
🔹 “I will come.” → He said he would come.

⚠ Backshift is not always necessary when the information remains true or the reporting context requires the original tense.

title: SEQUENCE OF TENSES
notes:
✓ Sequence of tenses → tense relationships between clauses, especially when one clause reports, explains, or depends on another.

◆ Present reporting verb → original tense often remains.
She says, “I am tired.” → She says that she is tired.

◆ Past reporting verb → tense may shift backward.
She said, “I am tired.” → She said that she was tired.

✓ Common shifts → Present Simple → Past Simple | Present Continuous → Past Continuous | Present Perfect → Past Perfect | Past Simple → Past Perfect | Will → Would.

⚠ Universal truths may remain in Present Simple.
🔹 The teacher said that water boils at 100°C.

title: COMMON TENSE ERRORS
notes:
❌ He go to school every day.
✓ He goes to school every day.

❌ She don't understand.
✓ She doesn't understand.

❌ Does he works here?
✓ Does he work here?

❌ Did you went there?
✓ Did you go there?

❌ I am know the answer.
✓ I know the answer.

❌ I have seen him yesterday.
✓ I saw him yesterday.

❌ She has went home.
✓ She has gone home.

❌ I am study now.
✓ I am studying now.

❌ He was play football.
✓ He was playing football.

❌ They had ate before we arrived.
✓ They had eaten before we arrived.

❌ If it will rain, we will stay home.
✓ If it rains, we will stay home.

❌ I have lived here since five years.
✓ I have lived here for five years.

❌ I have lived here for 2020.
✓ I have lived here since 2020.

title: THE 12 TENSE FORMULA TABLE
notes:
◆ PRESENT
1. Simple → S + V1/V1+s(es)
2. Continuous → S + am/is/are + V-ing
3. Perfect → S + have/has + V3
4. Perfect Continuous → S + have/has + been + V-ing

◆ PAST
5. Simple → S + V2
6. Continuous → S + was/were + V-ing
7. Perfect → S + had + V3
8. Perfect Continuous → S + had + been + V-ing

◆ FUTURE
9. Simple → S + will + V1
10. Continuous → S + will + be + V-ing
11. Perfect → S + will + have + V3
12. Perfect Continuous → S + will + have + been + V-ing.

title: TENSE SIGNAL WORDS: MASTER LIST
notes:
◆ Present Simple → always, usually, normally, often, sometimes, rarely, never, every day, every week.

◆ Present Continuous → now, right now, at the moment, currently, today, these days.

◆ Present Perfect → already, just, yet, ever, never, recently, lately, so far, until now, since, for.

◆ Present Perfect Continuous → for, since, all day, lately, recently, how long.

◆ Past Simple → yesterday, last week, last year, ago, in 2010, when I was young.

◆ Past Continuous → while, when, as, at that moment, at 8 p.m. yesterday.

◆ Past Perfect → before, after, already, by the time, until then.

◆ Past Perfect Continuous → for, since, before, until, by the time.

◆ Future Simple → tomorrow, soon, later, next week, next year, in the future.

◆ Future Continuous → this time tomorrow, at 8 tomorrow, next week at this time.

◆ Future Perfect → by, by then, by tomorrow, by next year, by the time.

◆ Future Perfect Continuous → for, since, by, by the time, by next year.

title: MASTER TENSE DECISION GUIDE
notes:
◆ Is it a habit, fact, routine, or state? → Present Simple.

◆ Is it happening around now or temporarily? → Present Continuous.

◆ Is a past action connected to the present? → Present Perfect.

◆ Is duration the main focus up to now? → Present Perfect Continuous.

◆ Is the action completed at a definite past time? → Past Simple.

◆ Was it in progress at a particular past time? → Past Continuous.

◆ Did it happen before another past event? → Past Perfect.

◆ Did it continue for a period before another past event? → Past Perfect Continuous.

◆ Is it a spontaneous decision, promise, offer, or prediction? → Will.

◆ Is it a future action in progress at a particular time? → Future Continuous.

◆ Will it be completed before a future deadline? → Future Perfect.

◆ Will it continue for a duration up to a future point? → Future Perfect Continuous.

◆ Is it a planned intention or evidence-based prediction? → Going to.

◆ Is it a fixed personal arrangement? → Present Continuous.

◆ Is it an official timetable or schedule? → Present Simple.

title: FINAL EXAM REVIEW
notes:
✓ Tense expresses time and aspect.

✓ English commonly teaches 12 tense combinations: 3 times × 4 aspects.

✓ Simple → facts, habits, events, states.

✓ Continuous → actions in progress or temporary situations.

✓ Perfect → earlier action connected to a reference point.

✓ Perfect Continuous → duration/process leading to a reference point.

✓ Present → current or general time.

✓ Past → earlier time.

✓ Future → later time.

✓ V1 = base verb; V2 = past form; V3 = past participle; V-ing = -ing form.

✓ Do/does/did → followed by V1.

✓ Have/has/had → followed by V3 in Perfect forms.

✓ Be + V-ing → Continuous forms.

✓ Will + V1 → Future Simple.

✓ Will + have + V3 → Future Perfect.

✓ Will + have + been + V-ing → Future Perfect Continuous.
